name: Spring Onion

basicInfo.description: Spring onions, also called scallions or green onions, are fast-growing and versatile. Both the green tops and the small white bulbs are edible.
whyGrow: Harvest in as little as 4–6 weeks
Use both greens and bulbs in cooking
Grow easily in containers or small spaces
basicInfo.water: Keep soil evenly moist, water lightly but regularly

growingSteps: Sow seeds 1 cm deep in rows
Water regularly to keep soil moist
Harvest young onions when stems are thick enough

careCalendar.description: Plant seeds 1 cm deep in rows.
Leave 5–10cm spacing between the strongest seedlings.
Cut greens or pull small onions as needed.
Harvest regularly to encourage more shoots.

harvestingGuide: Harvest spring onions when stems reach pencil thickness. Pull the whole plant or cut leaves 2–3cm above the base to regrow. Continuous harvesting keeps them productive.
estimatedSavings: Growing spring onions can save $20–40 per season, as supermarket bunches cost $2–3 and fresh harvest lasts for months.
